title: Interchanging proper direct image and extension by zero
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and let $\Lambda$ be admissible in the sense of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use the finite-subextension condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], as fixed by the chapter. Let $p:\overline X\to Y$ be proper, let
$i:Y\to\overline Y$ be a quasi-compact open immersion, and let
$\overline X\xrightarrow{j'}W\xrightarrow{r}\overline Y$ be a compactification of
$i\circ p$ in the sense of [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], with $\overline X$ dense in $W$. Then:

1. $r^{-1}(Y)=\overline X$ (as open subschemes of $W$), and $r$ restricts to $p$
over $Y$;
2. for $A\in D(\overline X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ there is a unique map
$\iota_A:i_!Rp_*A\to Rr_*j'_!A$ in $D(\overline Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ whose
restriction to $Y$ is the identity of $Rp_*A$;
3. $\iota_A$ is an isomorphism for every $A\in\Loc(\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda))$.

proof.text: Since $rj'=ip$, $j'$ factors through the open subscheme $V=r^{-1}(Y)$. The morphism $V\to Y$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence separated by the definition of proper in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The induced $Y$-morphism $\overline X\to V$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated], and has closed image by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]. It is an open immersion, since it is the restriction of the open immersion $j'$ to an open containing its image. Its image is dense in $V$: every nonempty open of $V$ is an open of $W$ and meets the dense image of $\overline X$. A closed dense subset is all of $V$. Thus this surjective open immersion identifies $\overline X$ with $r^{-1}(Y)$ as open subschemes, not merely as sets, and $r$ restricts to $p$.

We first establish open restriction for the derived direct image in the actual coefficient category. All rings on the corners are the pullbacks of the same condensed $\Lambda$. Clause (1) of the current [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] gives the ring isomorphisms $\alpha_f:f^{-1}\Lambda_{\mathrm{target}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{\mathrm{source}}$, and its final assertion makes module pullback exact: it is canonically naturally isomorphic to the lift of $f^{-1}$ with action transported along $\alpha_f^{-1}$. We use that natural isomorphism, not a literal equality of the module functors with sheaf inverse image. The admissible coefficients here use precisely its finite-subextension condensed $\Qlb$ convention. Only the untwisted assertions are used; the new Tate-twist hypotheses play no role. On module sheaves, [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf](1),(4), applied to the Cartesian square of step 1, supplies the exact open adjunctions and $r^*i_!\simeq j'_!p^*$. Apply these exact functors termwise. They descend through quasi-isomorphisms and give triangulated functors by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]; the termwise units and counits descend too, and their triangle identities remain identities, giving $i_!\dashv i^*$ and $j'_!\dashv j'^*$ on the unbounded derived categories. The adjunctions $p^*\dashv Rp_*$ and $r^*\dashv Rr_*$ are [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with $Lf^*=f^*$ by exactness. For $T\in D(Y,\Lambda)$ and $B\in D(W,\Lambda)$ the successive adjunctions therefore give natural bijections
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(T,i^*Rr_*B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_!T,Rr_*B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(r^*i_!T,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j'_!p^*T,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(p^*T,j'^*B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,Rp_*j'^*B).
$$
These identify $i^*Rr_*B$ with $Rp_*j'^*B$: apply the bijections and their inverses to the two identity maps; naturality shows that the resulting two arrows compose to the identities. This proves the required derived restriction formula without substituting a ringed-space theorem for a ringed-topos theorem.

source.place: Proof (2): restriction via exact open adjunction and its base-change isomorphism.

proof.text: For $B=j'_!A$ the unit isomorphism $j'^*j'_!A\simeq A$ of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf](1) and step 2 give a natural identification $i^*Rr_*j'_!A\simeq Rp_*A$. Under the derived adjunction $i_!\dashv i^*$ constructed in step 2, a map $i_!Rp_*A\to Rr_*j'_!A$ corresponds to its restriction composed with the unit $Rp_*A\to i^*i_!Rp_*A$, which is an isomorphism by the same node. Choose the map corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{Rp_*A}$. The bijection proves existence and uniqueness. This defines $\iota_A$ for every unbounded $A$. Write $F=i_!Rp_*$ and $G=Rr_*j'_!$. For $f:A\to A'$, both $G(f)\circ\iota_A$ and $\iota_{A'}\circ F(f)$ restrict to $Rp_*(f)$ under the natural identification of step 2; the same adjunction bijection, now between $F(A)$ and $G(A')$, makes them equal. For an integer $n$, identify $F(A[n])$ with $F(A)[n]$ and $G(A[n])$ with $G(A)[n]$ using the derived shift isomorphisms. The shifted map $\iota_A[n]$ and $\iota_{A[n]}$ then both restrict to the identity of $Rp_*(A[n])$: the open base-change isomorphism and units in step 2 are termwise maps, so commute with these shifts. Uniqueness gives their equality, proving compatibility with shifts as well as naturality.

source.place: Proof (2): identity under the open adjunction.

proof.text:
First take $A\in\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda)$. By [det-proper-image-localizing-open], $j'_!A\in\Dctf(W,\Lambda)$. Let $c:Z\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ be the closed complement of $Y$, let $W_Z=W\times_{\overline Y}Z$, and write $c':W_Z\to W$ and $r_Z:W_Z\to Z$. These are again schemes and morphisms of the standing setting. Proper base change gives
$$c^*Rr_*j'_!A\simeq R(r_Z)_*c'^*j'_!A.$$
For finite $\Lambda$ this is clause (2) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite]. For $\mathcal O_E$ it is clause (3) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral], and for $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ clause (3) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational]. The latter two apply since $\Dctf\subset\Dbc$ by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; the cases $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$ are $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. By step 1, $W_Z$ misses $\overline X$. Clause (4) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] applied to $j'$ and $c'$ now identifies $c'^*j'_!$ with extension from the empty open, hence with zero (the sheaf axiom for the empty cover makes every module sheaf on the empty scheme zero). The same clause applied to $i$ and $c$ gives $c^*i_!=0$. Thus both restrictions of $\iota_A$ to $Z$ are maps between zero objects; its restriction to $Y$ is the identity by step 3.

source.place: Proof (3): proper base change and vanishing on the closed complement.

proof.text: The restrictions $i^*$ and $c^*$ are exact by the final untwisted assertion of the current [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], with coefficient actions transported along the inverse ring comparisons as in step 2. The cone of $\iota_A$ for $A\in\Dctf$ therefore has cohomology sheaves whose two restrictions vanish, by step 4. Each such sheaf is zero by [lem-exc-open-closed-detection], so the cone is acyclic and $\iota_A$ is an isomorphism. For the extension to $\Loc(\Dctf)$ use [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] first with compactification $(\mathrm{id}_{\overline X},p)$ to obtain exactness and coproduct preservation for $Rp_*$, then with $(i,\mathrm{id}_{\overline Y})$ for $i_!$, and with $(j',r)$ for $Rr_*j'_!$. Thus both functors $i_!Rp_*$ and $Rr_*j'_!$ have the hypotheses of [det-sf-determination-localizing]. The natural transformation $\iota$ commutes with shifts by step 3. Its invertibility locus contains $\Dctf$ by the preceding argument, so that cited determination lemma implies it contains all of $\Loc(\Dctf)$.

source.place: Proof (3): detection and propagation through localizing closure.

proof_origin.place: Proof clauses (1)--(3); the open restriction formula is expanded using the open base-change isomorphism and adjunction bijections.

split_report.summary: Completed the existing sandbox split without new nodes. Fixed imported-node blueprint.from, replaced an inapplicable ringed-space restriction citation by a fully written adjunction calculation on ordinary pro-etale module derived categories, justified closed-complement vanishing by open base change, and made all three applications of the compactification functor lemma explicit. The standing-setting and admissible-coefficient conventions are named. All five steps have verbatim statement quotations for every cited input. Repair of landing L: rebased the retained split onto the current authoritative item metadata, re-read all 19 step/input statement pairs, replaced both obsolete Cartesian-coefficient quotations, and adjusted steps 2 and 5 to use its precise canonical lift and untwisted exactness assertion. The finite-subextension condensed Qlb convention agrees with the coefficients used here; no Tate-twist assertion is needed. The coefficient-definition comparison exposed an ambiguity in the imported Qlb convention; the statement now explicitly names the finite-subextension condensed ring fixed by the chapter, without identifying it with the larger topological condensed ring.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the blueprint proof clauses (1), (2), and (3), with clause (3) split into the Dctf closed-complement argument and the localizing-category propagation.

reviewed.note:
mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q47-dff6a202e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 5 steps and every cited statement in full, against the main-20261015 blueprint statement and proof and Stacks 09AH (proetale.tex lemma-ses-associated-to-open, line 5135; it needs a quasi-compact open, which holds). There are no new nodes. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. A dependency search finds no cycle. No SGA is cited.

Statement: clauses 1-3 match the blueprint word for word. The two additions only fix the chapter's own setting and do not weaken anything: (a) the standing separated finite-type setting, which every coefficient-specific input already requires; (b) for Qlb, the finite-subextension ring of sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, which the chapter's layer B cites and which sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients and the rational proper base change node use. I checked the convergent-sequence example: the two condensed rings differ, and the item does not claim they are equal.

Step 1: proper base change, proper implies separated, proper into a separated target, and closed image, plus density, give r^{-1}(Y)=Xbar as open subschemes. Step 2: clause (4) of the ring-sheaf node applies (qcqs schemes, i quasi-compact, U' = Xbar by step 1); the termwise exact adjunctions descend, and the six Hom bijections give i^*Rr_*B = Rp_*j'^*B. Step 3: since the unit of i_! -| i^* is invertible, existence, uniqueness, naturality and shift compatibility follow; this step is genuinely elementary. Step 4: j'_!A is in Dctf(W), and Dctf is contained in Dbc. The finite clause (2), integral clause (3) and rational clause (3) of proper base change cover A, Z_l, O_E, Q_l, E and Qlb. Clause (4) of the ring-sheaf node with an empty open gives both vanishings over the closed complement. Step 5: the open/closed detection lemma kills each cohomology sheaf of the cone. det-sf-comp-coherence-single is applied three times, to (id,p), (i,id) and (j',r), and every hypothesis holds. The localizing determination lemma then gives the isomorphism on all of Loc(Dctf).

Edge cases checked: all maps identities; p=id with W=Ybar; Y empty; A=0. Without the density hypothesis clause 1 fails.

Tool uses for L: the worker's five, plus det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-{finite,integral,rational}. These give the Dctf case of the blueprint's cited sk-prop-proper-base-change-unbounded, which has no realized node; only the Dctf case is needed.

For maintenance: the literal wording of sk-def-localizing-closure gives the larger ring C(-,Qlb), so it should be aligned with the chapter's convention. The stored unit record still carries the old sec-smooth-purity text.
